newsitem.title: CUBA: U.S. hurricane aid set to go to central Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hurricane aid set to go to central Cuba.

text.p: A shipment of food aid sent to Cuba by Cuban-American donors in the United States for victims of Hurricane Lili is set to be transported soon to central Cuba, a U.S. Roman Catholic Church official said on Monday.

Father Thomas Wenski, an official from the Miami archdiocese who travelled with the planeload of aid from Miami to Havana on Saturday, told Reuters the food was currently stored in a warehouse in Havana.
It would be loaded onto trucks, probably on Monday, and taken by road to the central city of Cienfuegos, where church officials have identified more than 10,000 needy people, Wenski said.

The 70,000 lbs (32,000 kg) of rice, beans and milk powder was channelled through the archdiocese of Miami and is being handled in Cuba by church charity, Caritas. The Miami church has assembled more food aid to be sent on another flight to Cuba, possibly this week.

Wenski, director of relief in the Miami archdiocese, said that although some of the boxes of food had been adorned with the words "Love can do everything", and "exile", this did not appear to pose a problem for authorities.
Caritas said last week that the government had made clear that aid could not be delivered from Miami if adorned with political slogans.
Hurricane Lili hit central and western Cuba 10 days ago. Authorities said it destroyed 5,000 homes and caused extensive damage to crops and power lines.
The Cuban American community in Miami rapidly mobilised to send aid, but some argued that assistance should not be sent as it would only prop up the government of President Fidel Castro.
Washington last week waived a ban on direct flights from the United States to Cuba to allow aid to reach Havana.
